column2: Abandoning vessels, by smearing the floor for three days one becomes pure. One should not have a dead Brahmin carried by a Shudra when his own people are present.
One should take the corpse after it is bathed and worshipped, and cremate it with flowers. One should not cremate a naked body; one should not leave behind any part of the body.
One of the same gotra should take it and place it on the pyre. One who kept sacred fires should be cremated by rule with three fires;
one who kept none with one worldly fire and another: "From this you were born; from you may he be born again."
This one for the heavenly world — the son should give the fire of comfort. The kin pour water once with name and gotra.
Thus the water-rite for the maternal grandfather, teacher and dead; desire-water for a friend's ghost, sister's son, mother-in-law and priest.
Apo nah shoshuchat agham — the son should offer for ten days. Ten pindas for a Brahmin; twelve are remembered for a Kshatriya;
fifteen for a Vaishya; thirty are declared for a Shudra. A son, or daughter's son, or another should give pinda like a son.
Having bitten neem leaves at the door of the house, composed, having rinsed, touched fire, water, cow-dung and white mustard,
they should enter slowly placing the foot on a stone, eating food without salt and alkali, without meat, sleeping on the ground,
eating bought or obtained food, bathed; the original performer does the ten days. In his absence a student should do the pinda and water and the rest.
As this death-impurity is prescribed for sapindas, so for birth too, for those wishing perfect purity.
For all the death-impurity; the birth-impurity of father and mother: the birth-impurity is the mother's alone; the father is pure after touching water.
On the day of a son's birth an ancestral rite is to be done — so determined; that day, for giving, cows, gold, garments and the like.
Death by death, birth-impurity by birth-impurity; of both, whichever is earlier, by that impurity he is purified.
If a death occurs in birth-impurity, or birth-impurity in a death, then taking the death-impurity as primary one should do the purification, not the birth.
Equal light impurity one should end by the first; unequal by the second, as the king of Dharma's word.
When a death comes within a death one is purified by the earlier impurity; the heavy overrides the light, but the light does not the heavy.
If another comes in the middle of the night in death- or birth-impurity, they are purified by the remainder; if in the remainder of the night more than two days;
if impurity occurs in the morning they are purified in three days. In both ten days, the family's food is not eaten.
Giving and the like should stop; the family's food is not eaten. If unknown, no sin the first; for the eater otherwise one day.
By great favor, for the ghost and for the fallen, the Narayana-bali is to be done; by it he obtains favor.
The lotus-eyed is imperishable; what is given there is not lost. Since he saves from falling, therefore Janardana is the worthy vessel.
For those who fall, Hari alone surely gives enjoyment and liberation. Seeing people dying, one should practice dharma as a helper.
Even a dead kinsman cannot follow a dead man; except for the wife, the way of Yama divides for all.
Dharma alone goes with him wherever he goes. One should do tomorrow's work today, the afternoon's in the forenoon;
Death does not wait for what is done or not done. For the one attached to field, shop and house, with mind gone elsewhere,
Death takes him and goes like a she-wolf reaching a bunch of grass. None is dear to Time and none hated by it.
When the action that grants life is exhausted, it seizes a person by force. One whose time has not come does not die, though pierced by hundreds of arrows;
one whose time has come does not live even when touched by a kusha tip. Neither medicines nor mantras save one joined with death.
Natural action finds its doer surely like a calf its mother. The world begins unmanifest, is manifest in the middle, and ends unmanifest;
as childhood and the rest occur in the body, so the arrival of another body; as one takes a new garment, so the embodied one a body.
This embodied one is eternal and cannot be killed; therefore one should abandon grief.
With pure feeling one should practice dharma in whatever stage one delights; equal to all beings; a mark is not the cause of dharma.
The fruit of the kataka tree clarifies water, though the water is not clarified merely by taking its name.
Straightforward, impotent, lame, blind and deaf — a twice-born is freed by the good; by ignorance he is bound in the world.
Whatever creatures an ascetic harms by ignorance by day and night, for purification of them he should bathe and do six breath-controls.
The bone-pillared body bound with sinews, plastered with flesh and blood, covered with skin, foul-smelling, full of urine and feces,
beset with old age and grief, a house of disease, afflicted, menstrual, impermanent, a dwelling for beings — one should abandon it.
Steadiness, forbearance, self-control, non-stealing, purity, control of the senses, modesty, learning, truth, non-anger — the ten marks of dharma.
Of four kinds is the mendicant: Kutichaka, Bahudaka, Hamsa and Paramahamsa; each later is better.
Single-staffed or triple-staffed, the yogi is freed from bondage. Non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy and non-possession,
the five Yamas; then the Niyamas: purity, contentment, austerity, study and worship of the Lord; the ascetic's seat is the lotus and the rest.
Breath-control is twofold: with seed and without seed. With repetition and meditation is with seed; the reverse is without seed.
Each of these is threefold: by inhalation, retention and exhalation. Inhalation from filling the breath; retention from its steadiness;
exhalation from breathing out; and by difference of measure threefold: twelve, twenty-four, and another of thirty-six measures.
A beat is the measure of a short syllable; one should slowly begin with Om. Withdrawal is for reciters; meditation is contemplating the Lord;
concentration is the steadiness of mind; samadhi is abiding in Brahman. This Self is supreme Brahman, truth, knowledge, infinite,
knowledge-bliss Brahman; "That thou art; I am that." Supreme Brahman, light, the Self, Vasudeva, free — Om.
Free of body, senses, mind, intellect, breath and ego, Brahman the fourth, free of waking, dream, deep sleep and the rest;
eternal, pure, awake, true, bliss, non-dual; "I am Brahman, supreme light, imperishable, all-pervading, Hari."
That Person in the sun, that I am, undivided, Om. Renouncing all undertakings, equal in pain and pleasure, forbearing,
pure in feeling, a man breaks through the cosmic egg and becomes Brahman. On the full moon of Ashadha one should observe the Chaturmasya vow;
then one should go out on the ninth and the rest, shaving at the junctures of seasons. For ascetics the atonement is meditation and breath-control.
Apastamba, Ushanas, Vyasa, Katyayana, Brihaspati, Gautama, Shankha and Likhita — as these spoke dharma,
so I shall tell briefly, giving enjoyment and liberation; hear. Vedic action is twofold: engaged and withdrawn;
desire-based action is engaged; withdrawn is preceded by knowledge. Study of the Veda, austerity, knowledge, restraint of the senses,
non-violence and service of the teacher bring the supreme good. Of all these, knowledge of the Self is declared supreme;
that is foremost of all knowledges; from it immortality is attained. Seeing the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self,
equal-minded, the self-sacrificer attains self-rule. In knowledge of the Self and evenness and in study of the Veda one should be diligent;
this is the capacity of the twice-born, especially of a Brahmin. Knowing the truth of Veda and scripture, living in whatever stage,
staying in this very world he becomes fit for becoming Brahman. The opening of Vedic study is on the full moon of Shravana, with Shravana;
in Hasta, on the day of herbs, or on the fifth of Shravana; or in Pausha on Rohini, or on Ashtaka,
at the water's edge one should do the closing of the meters outside by rule. For three days no study for the dead — disciples, priests, teachers, kin;
at the opening and closing, and for a Shrotriya of one's own branch; in the roar of twilight, a thunderclap, earthquake, falling meteor,
having completed the Veda and read the Aranyaka continuously, on the fifteenth, fourteenth, eighth, at Rahu's birth,
at the junctures of seasons, after eating or accepting ancestral-rite food; between animals, frogs, mongooses, dogs, snakes, cats and boars,
for a day and night, at the fall of Indra's banner, at the sound of a dog, jackal, ass, owl, ...
near the impure, a corpse, a Shudra, outcaste, cremation ground and fallen persons; under inauspicious stars; in a flood of lightning and thunder;
after eating, with wet hands, in the water, at midnight, in a great wind, rain of dust, burning of directions, in twilight, fog and fear,
for one running, in harm to creatures, when a distinguished guest comes, on climbing an ass, camel, vehicle, elephant, horse, boat or tree —
thirty-seven non-study occasions, these are the temporary ones, they know.
one should make four vessels with scented water and sesame; into the arghya ancestor-vessels one should sprinkle the ghost's vessel
with the two verses "Ye samanah"; the rest as before. This is the Sapindikarana; the Ekoddishta with women.
If the Sapindikarana of someone is done earlier than a year, for him too one should give food with a water-pot to a Brahmin for a year.
On the death day one should do it every month for a year; every year the rite is to be done like the monthly food.
With haviṣya food for a month, with pudding for a year; with fish, deer, black antelope, birds, goat and spotted deer,
with the flesh of spotted deer, Raurava deer, boar and hare in order; with increase of months the grandfathers are satisfied by what is given.
Rhinoceros flesh, great shalka fish, food with honey, iron-flesh, kalashaka, and the flesh of the Vardhrinasa bird —
what one gives at Gaya is all called endless; likewise on the thirteenth in the rainy season and in Magha, no doubt.
Daughters, offspring, bards, chief cattle, sons, ghee, agriculture and trade, cloven-hoofed and one-hoofed,
sons of Brahmin splendor, gold and silver and base metals, eminence among kin — the giver of ancestral rites always obtains all desires.
From pratipada onward, excepting the fourteenth; for those slain by weapon it is given there.
Heaven, offspring, vigor, valor, land, strength, eminent sons, good fortune, offspring, leadership, sons,
a continuing line of sons, trade, children, health, fame, freedom from grief, the supreme goal,
wealth, learning, physician's success, silver, cows, goats and sheep, horses and life — whoever duly gives the ancestral rite
from Krittika to the end of Bharani obtains these desires. The ancestors, sons of Vasus, Rudras and Aditi, are the deities of the rite;
satisfied by the ancestral rite they please men's ancestors. Life, offspring, wealth, knowledge, heaven, liberation and pleasures
they grant, and kingdom; pleased, the grandfathers of men.
jaggery rice, pudding, haviṣya, milk rice, curd rice, oblation, cakes, meat, and varied foods.
